papers.title: Faster algorithms and a smaller kernel for Cliques or Trees Vertex Deletion
papers.abstract: In the Cliques or Trees Vertex Deletion (COTVD) problem, we are given an n-vertex graph G and an integer k, and we ask whether there is a vertex set of size at most k whose removal makes the resulting graph a disjoint union of cliques and trees. This problem is known to be fixed-parameter tractable and admits a kernel of size O(k^2). We improve this result by giving a kernel of size O(k), as well as an O(1.618^k n^{O(1)}) time algorithm, improving upon the previous O(1.75^k n^{O(1)}) time algorithm. The kernelization relies on a refined analysis of the structure of graphs that are no-instances, and a new reduction rule based on packing subgraphs.
